This means that chat participants may see deviating orders of messages, replies to messages they don't even see. In theory, it's even possible that several messages from the same sender arrive and are displayed in wrong order.  Idea 1: Sort the conversation view by "sent" timestamp. See also Display send date for incoming messages #806. Problem: What is the "sent" date? Is it reliable? Is it set by the client or the TS server (farm)? Idea 2: Give each message a sequence number generated by the TextSecure server. Sort conversation view according to those numbers. Problem: Many, but not all messages go through the TS server. Idea 3: Employ vector clocks.

<MISSING_SCOPE>, <MISSING_CONDITION>, the App must sort the "conversation view" by "sent" time.
<MISSING_SCOPE>, <MISSING_CONDITION>, the App must display the "messages" in the "conversation view" in the same order for all "chat participants".

requirements.nl_text: Request Number - 7345 | Request Title - Better Media Saving Behavior | Request Description - I have:   searched open and closed issues for duplicates  read https://github.com/WhisperSystems/Signal-Android/wiki/Submitting-useful-bug-reports  Bug description. One of the features that was missing for a long time but thankfully has been recently implemented was the ability to swipe through the images without having to keep going back to the index and always having it start at the top. Kudos and thanks for that. However, another element exists that can be greatly improved and probably just got missed; and hopefully can be added. Currently each picture ("media") provides you the save button on the top. However, it never detects that the item has already been saved and you have to just remember it or go check your on device gallery to see if it is already there. Instead, it simply keeps making duplicates of the item and just incrementing it. It would't be too difficult to do a simple if/exists > show view/share icon else/doesn't > show save icon (as it is now). This will spare the need to save multiple duplicates and incrementing it when you can simply provide a visual check that it has already been saved. It is simply better UX and cleaner that way. Steps to reproduce.  save an item save it again you have a duplicate with a -1 at the end save it again you now have 3 with a -1 and -2 of the same item repeat and goes on as long as you keep saving Expected result: Detect that the item has already been saved and either provide a view icon or share icon to visually indicate it has been saved already, otherwise show the save button. A simple file system check for the item will facilitate this. Thanks in advance.
human_rimays: <MISSING_SCOPE>, if the "media item" has already been saved, then the App must change the "save icon" to a "view/share icon".
<MISSING_SCOPE>, if a picture has already been saved, then the App must show a view or share icon instead of the save button.
<MISSING_SCOPE>, if the user has already saved a "media item", then the App must show a "view" or "share" icon instead of the "save" button.
requirements.llm_rimay: For each "media item", if the "media item" has already been saved to the device, then the Signal-Android application must display a "view icon" or a "share icon" in place of the "save button".

verdict.text:
## Summary
Zero-shot Sonnet produces conversions semantically close to the humans: cosine reaches 93% of the human-human ceiling. Its main weakness runs against the experiment's hypothesis. It does not fabricate actors; it over-flags them. In 10 of 29 implied-actor cases and 13 of 34 implied-modal cases it emits `<MISSING_ACTOR> <MISSING_MODAL_VERB>` where all annotators wrote "the App must". The headline scope/condition "silent fill" counts appear to be a scoring artifact.

## Missing-slot detection
Scope (32/34 "silently filled") and condition (18/21) dominate the 52 fills, but the outputs mostly contain no scope or condition at all. For example, 592, 8-Mastodon, 2943 and 4333 begin directly with the actor placeholder, yet they are labelled `filled`. The scorer is treating omission as filling. Only a few cases are real scope insertions:
- 828 ("For all the TextSecure groups")
- 1504 ("For individual contacts or groups")

Scope/condition recall therefore cannot be read as fabrication until absence is scored separately.

Actor and modalVerb show perfect recall on one gold-missing case each, which is meaningless at n=1. Precision is 0.07–0.09 because of the over-flagging above. Action is the only slot with real signal, and the sample is tiny (4):
- Correctly flagged: 83 and 1504.
- Filled: 592 and 496. The 496 fill is a plausible fabrication: it has the lowest similarity (0.18) yet passes Paska.

At requirement level, verdict recall is 3/4, but there are 11 false "incomplete" verdicts, all caused by actor/modal placeholders.

## Conversion quality
String metrics reach 72–78% of the ceiling, while cosine reaches 93%. The gap is largely surface form. Every human output carries the `<MISSING_SCOPE>, <MISSING_CONDITION>,` prefix; the LLM drops it, which penalises seq_ratio and Jaccard more than embeddings.

Paska's 46% pass rate is mostly downstream of the placeholder habit:
- All 14 LLM-"incomplete" outputs fail, mainly as "Not requirement", because Paska cannot find a system response without an actor.
- On LLM-complete outputs the pass rate is 76%.

Genuine stylistic smells are few:
- Condition after the response: 316 and 6459.
- Imprecise verb: 1283 and 7310.
- Two actions in one response: 6457.

## Anomalies
- Text outside the answer block, short (44–128 chars), in 175, 4031, 4230, 496, 5555, 6077 and 757. All were parsed and scored, and six of the seven pass Paska, so there is no visible distortion.
- An atomic requirement was flagged `<NON_ATOMIC>` in 2055. Its output also lacks an actor and fails Paska.
- Two undetected atomicity issues: 6459's Paska segment IDs reach `rimay_3`, suggesting a multi-sentence answer for an atomic requirement, and 6457 has a Paska non-atomic smell. The anomaly checker caught neither.

## Next step
- Fix the slot extractor to label an absent scope/condition as `omitted`, distinct from `filled`, then recompute Track 1. The current scope/condition numbers are not interpretable.
- Revise the zsl prompt so placeholders are reserved for genuinely missing content, and an implied system actor is written as "the App". Expect Paska pass rate and verdict precision to rise sharply.
- Extend the anomaly checker to count Rimay sentences per atomic answer (6459), then compare against fsl/cot before drawing strategy conclusions.
